## Conference overview

*Preview by Matt Youmans, p. 265. Reproduced in full.*


> It’s football season, yet the unveiling of a new-look Pac-12 Conference brings back memories of the late, great Bill Walton.

> The basketball legend and colorful broadcaster constantly touted the “conference of champions” due to the league’s impressive history of NCAA titles.

> Unfortunately, the schools responsible for almost all of those titles — Stanford, UCLA, USC, Cal, Oregon, Washington, Arizona and Arizona State — are long gone and spread to different conferences all over the map.

> Oregon State and Washington State, the league’s two leftovers, have been joined by a handful of newcomers from the Mountain West (Boise State, San Diego State, Colorado State, Fresno State and Utah State) and a straggler from the Sun Belt (Texas State).

> The Pac-12 consists of only eight teams and all include the name “State.” The conference will not get an automatic qualifier into the College Football Playoff.

> Boise State, which won the last three Mountain West championships, is listed by DraftKings as the +170 favorite to win the Pac-12.

> The Broncos could boast the conference’s top quarterback, Maddux Madsen, and top running back, Dylan Riley.

> San Diego State, the +370 second choice, went 9-4 last season and is led by workhorse running back Lucky Sutton.

> The league does present a few intriguing teams beyond the Broncos and Aztecs.

> In his first season at Fresno State, coach Matt Entz won nine games.

> Watch out for Entz and the Bulldogs, and keep an eye on Colorado State with new coach Jim Mora Jr., who worked an incredible turnaround at UConn.

> Texas State arrives with quarterback Brad Jackson triggering an explosive passing attack.

> The Pac-12 can make a statement, for better or worse, when Boise State opens its season at Oregon on Sept. 5.

> On the same day, Fresno State visits USC and Washington State plays at Washington.

> Other nonconference matchups to circle are San Diego State at UCLA (Sept. 12) and BYU at Colorado State (Sept. 19).

> In the biggest league games, Fresno hosts Boise on Oct. 10 and Boise hosts San Diego State on Nov. 21. pac-12

**From the team pages in this conference** — 8 of 8 teams' pages address this theme. A sample follows; Phase 3 carries the full treatment team by team.


- **Boise State Broncos** (p. 266) — Danielson has a senior quarterback and an experienced team that deserves to be the Pac12 favorite.

- **Colorado State Rams** (p. 268) — The change is unlikely to be sudden in Fort Collins because Mora must implement more than 60 new players on the roster, and he’s got some questions about the quarterback position.

- **Fresno State Bulldogs** (p. 270) — When projecting college football teams, it’s no secret the two most important positions of handicapping emphasis are the head coach and quarterback.

- **Oregon State Beavers** (p. 272) — It’s tempting to forecast Oregon State as a surprise team, with Murphy’s potential at quarterback and MacIntyre’s ability to build the defense.

- **San Diego State Aztecs** (p. 274) — He’s got to find the right quarterback to operate his system.

- **Texas State Bobcats** (p. 276) — Kinne is a former college and NFL quarterback who’s known for creating prolific passing offenses.

- **Utah State Aggies** (p. 278) — Mendenhall must replace a veteran quarterback, and he has settled on another veteran to lead the team into the Pac-12.

- **Washington State Cougars** (p. 280) — In 2022, a quarterback from Incarnate Word, an FCS program in San Antonio, transferred to Washington State.

## Historical and situational notes


**From the conference preview (p. 265):**

**From the team pages in this conference** — 8 of 8 teams' pages address this theme. A sample follows; Phase 3 carries the full treatment team by team.


- **Boise State Broncos** (p. 266) — The Broncos were a powerhouse two years ago, going 12-2 and reaching the College Football Playoff, so last season’s 9-5 finish was an obvious step back.

- **Colorado State Rams** (p. 269) — Farrar attempted 18 passes as a backup last season when the Huskies’ success had a lot to do with star quarterback Joe Fagnano, who finished with 28 touchdown passes and one interception.

- **Fresno State Bulldogs** (p. 270) — In 2025, he took over a Fresno State team that went 6-7 the previous season and guided the Bulldogs to a 9-4 finish punctuated by a win in the Arizona Bowl.

- **Oregon State Beavers** (p. 272) — Jonathan Smith had it rolling at Oregon State, posting 10 wins in 2022 and eight in 2023, but it seemed inevitable that he would leave for a big payday and he got it from Michigan State.

- **San Diego State Aztecs** (p. 274) — Sean Lewis predicted a quick turnaround when he took over a losing San Diego State team in 2024, but ugly losses piled up and he went 3-9.

- **Texas State Bobcats** (p. 277) — He completed 71.3% of his passes last season while totaling 3,224 yards and 21 touchdowns with seven interceptions.

- **Utah State Aggies** (p. 278) — Utah State is his third stop since leaving Provo in 2015, and he has had a losing record since ditching BYU.

- **Washington State Cougars** (p. 280) — In 2022, a quarterback from Incarnate Word, an FCS program in San Antonio, transferred to Washington State.
